title: Hills of SF 101
one_line_rule: Learn four facts about the city's hills, then practice them.

style.cover_prompt: chalk drawing of San Francisco's hills on a dark blue chalkboard, two rounded peaks and a winding street, soft chalk dust

lesson.title: Hills of SF 101
points: Twin Peaks is two summits side by side, near the middle of the city.
Lombard Street's famously crooked block winds down Russian Hill.
Coit Tower stands on top of Telegraph Hill, above North Beach.
Cable car lines climb up and over Nob Hill.

questions.q: Why is it called Twin Peaks?
questions.explain: Twin Peaks is two summits side by side, hence the name.

questions.q: Where in the city is Twin Peaks?
choices: Near the middle of the city
questions.explain: Twin Peaks rises near the center of San Francisco, so you can see most of the city from it.

questions.q: Lombard Street's crooked block is on which hill?
questions.explain: The famously crooked block of Lombard Street winds down Russian Hill.

questions.q: What makes that block of Lombard Street famous?
questions.explain: The street zigzags through tight switchbacks because the hill is too steep to drive straight down.

questions.q: Which tower stands on top of Telegraph Hill?
questions.explain: Coit Tower crowns Telegraph Hill; Sutro Tower is the tall antenna near Twin Peaks.

questions.q: Which neighborhood sits just below Telegraph Hill?
questions.explain: Telegraph Hill rises right above North Beach, near the waterfront.

questions.q: Which hill do cable car lines climb up and over?
questions.explain: Cable car lines run up and over Nob Hill on their way across downtown.

questions.q: How does a cable car get up a steep hill?
questions.explain: The car grips a cable that moves in a slot under the street, and lets go to stop.
